title: Eleven Landowners Still Unpaid When the Cap-Haïtien to Labadie Road Closed
place: The Cap-Haïtien to Labadie road, Bande du Nord, Nord department, Haiti

lenders.name: World Bank (IDA)
lenders.role: Grants IDA-H5510, IDA-H8120 and IDA-D1360 for the Infrastructure and Institutions Emergency Recovery Project (P120895), SDR 67.2 million, US$102.8 million equivalent in all: US$65 million under H5510, US$35 million under H8120 and US$2.8 million under D1360, of which US$100,526,845 was disbursed. Recipient the Republic of Haiti; implementing agency the Unité Centrale d'Exécution of the Ministry of Public Works, Transport and Communications. Environmental category A. Processed under OP 8.00, Rapid Response to Crises and Emergencies, after the January 2010 earthquake. Approved 18 March 2010, effective 23 April 2010, mid-term review 17 April 2012, original closing 30 June 2013, actual closing 29 June 2018. Additional financing was approved on 27 September 2012 under P130749 and a second on 10 November 2016 under P156049. Involuntary Resettlement (OP/BP 4.12), Environmental Assessment (OP/BP 4.01), Natural Habitats (OP/BP 4.04), Pest Management (OP/BP 4.09) and Physical Resources (OP/BP 4.11) were triggered. The completion report ICR00004504, dated 27 December 2018, rated outcome Moderately Satisfactory and quality of monitoring and evaluation Modest. It gives two different ratings for Bank performance: its key ratings page says Satisfactory and its paragraph 92 says "Rating Bank Performance: Moderately Satisfactory". The Independent Evaluation Group's review ICRR0021536 rated outcome and Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory and its table reports the completion report's own rating as Moderately Satisfactory, matching the report's paragraph 92 and not its key ratings page, under a comment reading "There is no discrepancy between IEG and ICR rating."

companies.name: Unité Centrale d'Exécution, Ministère des Travaux Publics, Transports et Communications
companies.role: The central implementation unit inside Haiti's public works ministry, named in the completion report's data sheet as the implementing agency and on the cover of the June 2018 resettlement plan as its author. It ran the resettlement, the census of affected people and the grievance mechanism, and continued to handle open cases under other Bank-financed projects after this one closed (Implementation Completion and Results Report, 27 December 2018; Plan d'Action de Réinstallation, June 2018).

companies.name: Comité Permanent d'Acquisitions à l'Amiable
companies.role: The Haitian government's land acquisition committee, which set the amounts owed to the people whose land was taken. The escrow account opened at the Banque de la République d'Haïti was provisioned in the amounts the committee set, as Haitian law provides (Implementation Completion and Results Report, 27 December 2018).

companies.name: Royal Caribbean
companies.role: The operator of the Labadie site. The June 2018 resettlement plan records that the extra kilometre of road added in September 2017, running to the Labadie landing stage, lies inside an existing right of way that is a concession from the Haitian state to Royal Caribbean, which operates the site, so no land along it was taken; an agreement was reached with the firm operating the site to move points of its metal fence where crossings were needed (Plan d'Action de Réinstallation, June 2018).

community:
The project rebuilt government buildings and infrastructure after the earthquake of 12 January 2010. Resettlement action plans were prepared for five separate works, and the completion report says they resulted in "the relocation of 12 households, land acquisition for 136 households, and non-land economic displacement of 223 households".

The project's social safeguard rating was Satisfactory or Moderately Satisfactory until December 2017, when it was cut to Moderately Unsatisfactory because compensation for land taken from 19 affected people for the Cap Labadie road works had not been paid. They were to have been paid by the government in April 2017. Eight were paid before the scheduled closing date of 29 June 2018. For the remaining 11 the government opened an escrow account at the Banque de la République d'Haïti, provisioned in the amounts set by the government's land acquisition committee, and the accounts are to stay in place for 30 years "to ensure consistency and that obligations can be fulfilled at any time during this period". The resettlement plan for the road was updated and re-disclosed on 25 June 2018, four days before closing, and the project was then closed procedurally. The safeguard rating was put back up to Moderately Satisfactory to reflect the opening of the account.

The June 2018 plan carries the payment record. For the original land acquisitions along the road it says the government paid 5,361,709.80 gourdes to twenty-six affected people, against a February 2015 valuation by the land acquisition committee covering twenty-six affectations and twenty-five people, listed plot by plot with the occupant's name. The nineteen still outstanding are the land taken for the additional works, the slope stabilisation and the outfall canals, which the committee's brigades surveyed between August and December 2017. The plan names the eight paid: cheques were issued for Myrtha Devalsaint, Victor Fadius Francius, Ethma Pierre, Lemercier Etienne, Delaleu Ardouin, Joseph Edwin, Colas Frantz and Regis Jude. It names nine whose expropriation procedures were still being finalised and gives the reason against each: for six, a file left incomplete with documents missing at 20 June 2018; for two, title still being checked by the tax authority; and for Amsterly Pierre, no document at all capable of establishing what he was claiming, after five recorded meetings and letters between October 2017 and 9 June 2018. Two further people were unidentified at 20 June 2018, their plots known only by road position and an estimated 204,000 and 144,000 gourdes. The plan tabulates the escrow sums for the eleven, from 48,060 gourdes to 2,643,300 gourdes, and records that none of the nine was displaced or lost an income-generating activity. For one of the three plots needed for the Ducroix variant the owner asked to be paid in kind, land for land, and the construction plan was changed to avoid the other two plots because their owners could not be found; a design choice made in September 2017 avoided moving one house and its toilet, so those two people were no longer affected.

The project also ran a grievance mechanism with regular open consultations at each site. The Independent Evaluation Group's review records that the project team told it that since the report was written 11 of the 19 affected people had been compensated and that the Bank was working with the authorities to compensate the remaining 8. That is a statement by staff rather than a document, and it reverses the split the completion report gives.
outcome: The grants closed on 29 June 2018, five years after the original closing date, with US$100,526,845 of US$102.8 million disbursed. Eleven of the nineteen people whose land was taken for the Cap Labadie road had not been paid, and their money, from 48,060 to 2,643,300 gourdes a case, sat in an escrow account at the central bank that is to remain available for 30 years. Two of the eleven were still unidentified and for the rest the plan records title documents missing or unverified. The Bank said its implementation support team had taken adequate precautions to bring the pending compensation to a close and that it would keep supervising open cases through other projects run by the same implementation unit. The completion report rated the outcome Moderately Satisfactory and the Independent Evaluation Group agreed.

title: Site engineer killed on the Lubuk Alung to Kuraitaji road works
place: Lubuk Alung to Kuraitaji road, Padang Pariaman, West Sumatra, Indonesia

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Project P090990, loan IBRD-80430 for the Western Indonesia National Roads Improvement Project, approved 26 May 2011, effective 12 March 2012, closed 30 June 2021 after four restructurings. The Bank's completion report of 14 December 2021 gives the loan as US$250 million originally, revised to US$228 million, with US$224,160,404 disbursed; its cover page states the amount as SDR 145.63 million. Environmental category B, partial assessment. Three safeguard policies were triggered, per the appraisal document's own table: environmental assessment OP 4.01, physical cultural resources OP 4.11 and involuntary resettlement OP 4.12. The same table marks natural habitats OP 4.04, forests OP 4.36, indigenous peoples OP 4.10 and safety of dams OP 4.37 as not triggered. The report rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory and the quality of monitoring and evaluation Substantial. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 7 June 2022 agrees on outcome and Bank performance but rates monitoring and evaluation Modest, giving shortcomings in its design as the reason. The two documents give different totals for what the project cost: the completion report's financing table gives US$224,160,404 both as the amount disbursed under the loan and as the total project cost, while the Evaluation Group's review prints US$223,780,891.76 as the total project cost and US$224,160,404.03 as the actual amount. Neither document explains the difference.

companies.name: Directorate General of Highways, Ministry of Public Works and Housing, Indonesia
companies.role: Implementing agency. The Directorate General of Highways is the national roads authority inside Indonesia's public works ministry; it ran the works through a project management unit and project implementation units in the provinces. The completion report does not name the supervision firm or the civil works contractor for package 21A.

community: The loan paid for widening and rehabilitating national road sections along the western Sumatra corridor, and later for road repairs in Central Sulawesi. The Bank's completion report records that a fatal traffic accident happened on road package 21A on 27 July 2019, in which a site engineer working for the project's design and supervision consultants was killed. The report gives the cause as human error, a car travelling at about 60 kilometres an hour hitting him from behind while he was taking photographs in the middle of the carriageway, and says the accident "could have been prevented if adequate traffic management provisions would had been deployed". Package 21A was the 16.23-kilometre Lubuk Alung to Kuraitaji section, a second contract procured to finish works left by package 21 on the same section, which the report says was terminated in June 2019 for the contractor's poor performance. The report's table of road packages gives 21A a commencement date of 3 January 2019 and a taking-over date of 1 July 2019, which is 26 days before the accident; the report does not explain how the two fit together. On land, the report says the involuntary resettlement policy was complied with, that land acquisition and resettlement plans were prepared and published for every road package, and that all affected people were paid at replacement cost on the basis of a valuation by a firm outside the project; the rating for social safeguards was raised from Moderately Satisfactory to Satisfactory in December 2018 after early delays. Twenty-four complaints were received and resolved over the life of the project, mainly about environmental and quality shortcomings, the last of them in October 2018.
outcome: The project closed on 30 June 2021. The completion report lists package 21A as completed. The Bank formally closed the fatality case in July 2020.
